awd_abstract_narration:
The conference "Hilbert Function Spaces 2025" will be held June 30-July 4, 2025 in Frascati, Italy, at a facility that belongs to the University “Tor Vergata” of Rome. The purpose of the meeting is for distinguished researchers in the field of Operator Theoretic Function Theory to share their recent progress during the plenary talks, for participants as a collective to work out the “state of the art” of the field, and to establish new collaborations among the participants. Funds from this grant will primarily be used to support the conference travel of US based early career mathematicians.  Participation in this conference will facilitate the integration of these individuals into the international research community in analysis, and it will inform and inspire their research and teaching efforts as they return to their home institutions in the US.
 
The conference will be an interdisciplinary workshop on Operator Theory, Function theory, and Harmonic Analysis, and their applications and interactions with other fields. These topics in pure mathematics are important parts of the foundations of the mathematics necessary for our modern digital devices such as cell phones and imaging devices, but they are also important in many other areas such as optimization and quantum physics. Information of the conference can be found at https://sites.google.com/view/hfs2025/home .

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
Hilbert Function Spaces 2025 was held June 30 - July 4, 2025, in Frascati, Italy, at a facility of the University of Rome Tor Vergata. The conference brought together researchers working in operator theory, function theory, harmonic analysis, and related areas of pure mathematics. These fields study abstract structures that underpin important areas of modern mathematics and have connections to signal processing, imaging, communications, optimization, and quantum physics. By supporting the exchange of new results and research ideas, the conference contributed to the development of mathematical knowledge that may support future scientific and technological advances.

Approximately 100 mathematical researchers attended, representing institutions in the United States, Europe, Asia, Africa, and Canada. The scientific program included 18 plenary lectures as well as 26 contributed talks. The invited speakers included internationally recognized researchers at different career stages, including both established and early-career mathematicians. Many of the talks presented recent research results, including work that had not yet been published. Conferences of this kind provide an important setting in which researchers first learn about new developments, exchange ideas, and identify opportunities for further research. In addition to the formal lectures, the meeting provided extensive opportunities for junior and senior researchers to discuss their work and establish professional connections.

The NSF award supported 13 participants affiliated with 10 U.S. universities in eight states. Five supported participants were graduate students, and five were postdoctoral researchers or other early-career mathematicians. The support reduced financial barriers to participation and enabled these researchers to take part in the international mathematical community. Their participation provided valuable exposure to current research, opportunities to interact with leading mathematicians, and experience presenting and discussing research. These benefits are expected to strengthen their future research and teaching activities and to contribute to the development of the U.S. mathematical workforce.
